scopeNotes: New text needs independent review; earlier hashes do not certify it.
Map endpoints are not historical founding or extinction dates.

Funj and funj-1783 are two existing imported map records with coverage1492–1530 and1783–1815. Both point to the Sultanate of Sennar, not two unrelated states. The c1504 conventional founding and1821 conquest differ from coverage endpoints. The earlier1492 snapshot is not silently validated as an established Funj state. No polygon, historical-basemap import or modern dataset is modified.

Most detailed domestic evidence here comes from Old Dongola, a northern local polity within the Funj sphere, not the capital Sennar. Local rulers and institutions are explicitly distinguished from the sultan. No claim makes the Dongola household sample representative of every community in the sultanate.

The2023 household article was read for setting, construction, compound organization, courtyard equipment and botanical remains. Relations between households and kinship are interpretive. Modern ethnographic accounts are not projected directly onto the past, nor are all food-preparation tasks attributed to women. The2024 households article already used on Makkura is not treated as this distinct2023 work.

The2021 excavation volume was downloaded in full as a298-page PDF. Pages6,95–101,152–155 and selected introductory material were read, not every chapter. The card uses U50’s dated storage deposit; observed order does not establish the reason it was left or the original contents of every vessel. The wooden key does not identify a particular lock. The broad date combines the report’s pottery and radiocarbon interpretations. Selected printed-page locators are retained.

The geophysical paper’s indexed methods and discussion were read; direct PMC access returned a challenge, and no bypass was attempted. Publication appeared online in2021 and in the2022 journal volume. Çelebi’s1672/1673 school count is explicitly a report transmitted through the study, not a modern archaeological census or evidence for universal attendance. The phrase Dark Ages in the original title describes gaps in research and is not adopted as a cultural judgment.

The2026 royal-order study was read in indexed publisher pages and author-uploaded text at https://www.researchgate.net/publication/400542022_The_King_of_Nubia_at_work_archaeological_context_and_text_edition_of_a_sixteenthseventeenth-century_Arabic_document_from_Old_Dongola . Direct publisher PDF access was blocked. Pages12–15 support the two-sided document and uncertain commodity terms. No exact reign, paper source, identity of every trader or fixed exchange price is fabricated. The study cautions that Qashqash may not uniquely identify one person across all literary sources. Local genealogy and the document’s exact relationship to later hagiography remain outside the card’s claims.

The dye paper’s abstract and conclusion were read. Its online announcement was in2023, journal publication2024. Dye identification and a probable fez fragment are attributed interpretations. Seventeen samples do not mean seventeen whole garments. Woad/indigo discrimination and precise geographical origin are not simplified into absolute identifications for every blue textile. The same source budget combines publisher and university versions.

The tobacco paper’s abstract and cultivation discussion were read. Its approximate1664–1760 evidence is not the first-ever use of the plant in Sudan. No health benefit, encouragement to smoke or assumption of universal practice is included.

The2025 pottery thesis is cited only from its public repository abstract; the listed PDF is embargoed until2031 and was not accessed. The abstract’s value ranking of wheel-made wares is not adopted. Its broad Islamic-period findings are not assigned to one precise Funj year.

Treccani supplies a concise secondary political outline, cross-checked against the excavation volume’s historical introduction. Spaulding1972 is used only from the publisher extract for uncertainty over early origins; competing ethnic-origin hypotheses are not asserted as settled. The1821 ending does not prove a specific successor map link. No successor target has been substituted solely on geography.

New prose is author-checked pending independent historical-depth review. Source and structural checks do not certify complete cultural coverage or border accuracy. No unsupported toilet, medicine or family custom has been invented to fill a topic.

proposedOverrides.summary: The Funj Sultanate ruled from Sennar in present-day Sudan. It developed in the early sixteenth century and lost independence to Turco-Egyptian conquest in 1821. The map shows separate snapshots of this history.

sharedAssociations.basis: Both imported IDs name Funj and have Sudanese Nile outlines corresponding to the early and later sultanate. The shared narrative distinguishes their map intervals from the conventional c1504 to1821 political history.
